Compute the joint site frequency spectrum of each pair of populations

Source: R/pairwise_pop_sfs.R
pairwise_pop_sfs.Rd

Compute the two-dimensional (joint) site frequency spectrum (SFS) of each pair of populations, i.e. the number of loci with \(i\) copies of the derived (or minor) allele in the first population and \(j\) in the second. Missing genotypes are dealt with as in easySFS, by projecting each population down to n_proj allele copies (see pop_sfs() for details). Each spectrum only uses the loci that have at least n_proj called allele copies in both its populations, so its marginal spectra are not, in general, equal to the spectra computed by pop_sfs(). A folded spectrum is folded on the total number of copies across the two populations (as in dadi), so that it counts copies of the allele that is the minor one across the pair.

Usage

pairwise_pop_sfs(.x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gen_tbl'
pairwise_pop_sfs(
  .x,
  n_proj = NULL,
  folded = TRUE,
  ancestral = NULL,
  type = c("tidy", "array"),
  fastest = c("last", "first"),
  n_cores = bigstatsr::nb_cores(),
  block_size = bigstatsr::block_size(nrow(.x), 1),
  ...
)

Arguments

.x

a grouped gen_tibble (as obtained by using dplyr::group_by()), with at least two groups.

...

other arguments passed to specific methods, currently unused.

n_proj

the number of allele copies to project each population to: either a single value used for all populations, a vector with one value per population (in the order of the groups), or a vector named with the group labels. If NULL (the default), each population is projected to the number of allele copies that maximises its number of segregating sites (see pop_sfs_preview()).

folded

boolean, whether to fold the spectrum (the default, as the ancestral allele is not usually known). If FALSE, the spectrum is polarised with ancestral.

ancestral

the ancestral allele of each locus, used to polarise unfolded spectra: either the name of a column of the loci table (see show_loci()), or a character vector with one allele per locus (in the order of the loci table). Loci whose ancestral allele is missing (NA) or is neither of their alleles are dropped. If NULL (the default), the reference allele is taken to be ancestral, as in easySFS. Ignored, with a warning, for folded spectra.

type

the type of object to return, either "tidy" (the default) or "array".

fastest

the order of the cells of each spectrum in the tidy output: "last" (the default) keeps the order of the populations, so that the rows are sorted by the number of allele copies in the first population, then in the second (the number of copies in the second population changes fastest, as in the files written by dadi and easySFS); "first" makes the number of copies in the first population change fastest.

n_cores

number of cores to be used, it defaults to bigstatsr::nb_cores()

block_size

maximum number of loci read at once.

Value

If type = "tidy", a tibble with one row per cell of the joint spectrum of each pair of populations, with the columns:

  • the groups of the pair (e.g. population_1 and population_2; one column per grouping variable for each population of the pair, if the data are grouped by more than one variable);

  • allele_count_1 and allele_count_2: the number of copies of the derived (or minor) allele in the first and second population (see allele_count in pop_sfs());

  • n_sites: the (projected) number of sites;

  • masked: whether the cell is masked (see pop_sfs()).

The projection of each population is stored in the attribute n_proj. The tibble has class pairwise_sfs_tbl, and can be plotted with autoplot(). If type = "array", a list of sfs objects (one per pair, named with the labels of the two groups pasted with "."), each an array with the first population in the rows and the second in the columns (see pop_sfs()). Pairs are in the order given by utils::combn().

See also

pop_sfs(), nwise_pop_sfs(), pop_sfs_preview()

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

example_gt %>% pairwise_pop_sfs(n_proj = 2)
#> # A tibble: 27 × 6
#>    population_1 population_2 allele_count_1 allele_count_2 n_sites masked
#>    <chr>        <chr>                 <int>          <int>   <dbl> <lgl> 
#>  1 pop1         pop2                      0              0   1.78  TRUE  
#>  2 pop1         pop2                      0              1   0.933 FALSE 
#>  3 pop1         pop2                      0              2   0.308 FALSE 
#>  4 pop1         pop2                      1              0   1.6   FALSE 
#>  5 pop1         pop2                      1              1   1.07  FALSE 
#>  6 pop1         pop2                      1              2   0     TRUE  
#>  7 pop1         pop2                      2              0   0.308 FALSE 
#>  8 pop1         pop2                      2              1   0     TRUE  
#>  9 pop1         pop2                      2              2   0     TRUE  
#> 10 pop1         pop3                      0              0   0.767 TRUE  
#> # ℹ 17 more rows

# as arrays
example_gt %>% pairwise_pop_sfs(n_proj = 2, type = "array")
#> $pop1.pop2
#> # A folded site frequency spectrum of 2 populations
#> # Allele copies: pop1 = 2, pop2 = 2
#> # Loci used: 6 (dropped for missing data: 0)
#>     pop2
#> pop1         0         1         2
#>    0 1.7833333 0.9333333 0.3083333
#>    1 1.6000000 1.0666667 0.0000000
#>    2 0.3083333 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> 
#> $pop1.pop3
#> # A folded site frequency spectrum of 2 populations
#> # Allele copies: pop1 = 2, pop3 = 2
#> # Loci used: 6 (dropped for missing data: 0)
#>     pop3
#> pop1         0   1         2
#>    0 0.7666667 1.8 0.3833333
#>    1 1.4666667 1.2 0.0000000
#>    2 0.3833333 0.0 0.0000000
#> 
#> $pop2.pop3
#> # A folded site frequency spectrum of 2 populations
#> # Allele copies: pop2 = 2, pop3 = 2
#> # Loci used: 6 (dropped for missing data: 0)
#>     pop3
#> pop2    0 1    2
#>    0 1.50 2 0.25
#>    1 1.00 1 0.00
#>    2 0.25 0 0.00
#>
